paper.abstract_en: This third part of the review article series 'Quantum Computing for Molecular Systems', discusses quantum algorithms. In particular, it focuses on the variational quantum algorithms (VQAs), which represent the most widely used class of quantum algorithms for near-term quantum devices. Building upon the mapping of fermionic Hamiltonians to qubit Hamiltonians (in Part II), here we explore how to employ VQAs to approximate the ground-state energy of molecular systems. We discuss the design of chemically motivated ansatzes, such as the unitary coupled-cluster approach, alongside hardware-efficient alternatives, highlighting trade-offs among expressibility, circuit depth, and resource requirements. We also elucidate the current hardware limitations, available quantum platforms, and hybrid quantum-classical approaches that are facilitating the early realization of quantum computing applications in molecular sciences.
